title: Trigonometry: Problems in Two and Three Dimensions
seo_title: Grade 12 Problems in 3D Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_text: Solve problems in two and three dimensions.
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 12 trigonometry worksheets: problems in two and three dimensions, cuboids, pyramids, lines and planes, elevation and bearings. 100 questions with memos.
key_sub: A vertical height is perpendicular to the ground.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Find a right-angled triangle that contains the unknown.
  • A vertical height is perpendicular to every line on the ground.
  • Use Pythagoras for lengths and sin, cos or tan for angles.
  • In a non-right-angled triangle, use the sine, cosine or area rule.

Examples

Example

cuboid 3 × 4 × 12

base diagonal √(9 + 16) = 5

space diagonal √(25 + 144)

Answer: 13

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
The wrong triangleDraw the triangle you need.
Sloping linesOnly lines on the ground are horizontal.
Hard methodsUse the right angle when there is one.
